fatal_errors: The proposed Hf-to-Al substitution does not reconstruct the target intervention of adding 4.2 at.% Cr.
The hypothesis assumes retention of a single-phase BCC structure, whereas the target mechanism requires approximately 4 vol.% of a reticulated multicomponent Laves phase.
The predicted strain-to-failure above 40% is inconsistent with the cited HfMoTaTiZr baseline and is unsupported by the supplied evidence.
The experiment does not specify a consistent loading mode, making tensile and compression fracture strains improperly interchangeable.
explanation: The proposal directly addresses density reduction and offers a controlled composition series with quantitative mechanical and density criteria, so it is a plausible alternative rather than unsupported. Evidence E2 supports the general proposition that Al can lower RHEA density and improve specific strength. However, it does not establish that Al-substituted HfMoTaTiZr will remain single-phase BCC, retain 1000 °C strength, or achieve greater than 40% failure strain. It misses the target Cr addition, lattice contraction, dislocation hardening, and the reticulated Cr2(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves-phase network responsible for simultaneous strength and ductility improvement. Its falsification rule is also overbroad: failure of the 15 at.% alloy would nominally reject a hypothesis stated for 5–10 at.% Al, and requiring every tested composition to satisfy all thresholds does not isolate the proposed optimum range.
